findings.reason: if an ensemble smoother already exists, §5 should extend it rather than stand up a parallel "windowed iterated ensemble smoother", and the author cannot make that call without the citation.
findings.text: §5–§7 propose new estimation machinery without citing the existing data-assimilation stack already in the tree, so the plan cannot show whether it rebuilds it: `imas_ambix/statespace/nova_ensemble_estimator.py:1` is literally "Nova-propagated ensemble conditioning with causal and smoothed products" (fixed-lag and full-sequence smoothing), `imas_ambix/statespace/sequential_da.py:1` is a sequential current-profile DA substrate, and `imas_ambix/statespace/enkf_baseline.py:1` is an EnKF baseline; none is named anywhere in §5.

findings.reason: a reuse claim with no file is the exact failure this rubric exists to catch; citing the encoder turns an assertion into a checkable extension target.
findings.text: §7 asserts the amortizer is "an extension of the absolute-geometry-token-substrate encoder … never a parallel module family" but names no code path, so the claim is unverifiable and the reuse it promises cannot be checked; the substrate lives in code at `imas_ambix/worldmodel/spacetime_relational_encoder.py` and `imas_ambix/tokenizer/patch_transformer.py` (per `docs/absolute-geometry-token-substrate.html`), and neither is cited.

findings.reason: either the plan should drive the existing in-tree solver or state the owner boundary that makes nova's the correct one; as written the plan waits on a capability it may already hold, which is a schedule decision the author would revisit.
findings.text: §4's dose-when and §5 both predicate the FF′ half on "the same nova free-boundary capability", yet the plan never reconciles that with the free-boundary Grad-Shafranov solver already in this repo, `imas_ambix/latent/gs_solve.py:1` ("Free-boundary Grad-Shafranov equilibrium solver — the force-balanced ψ decoder", free-boundary Picard with Green's-function boundary conditions from measured coil currents).

findings.reason: the eigenmodes are the mechanism §5 wants to estimate; the plan should extend `latent/temporal_operator.py` (the named owner) rather than introduce a second placeholder.
findings.text: §5's "2–4 vessel-current eigenmodes" duplicate infrastructure that exists: `temporal_operator.py:551` is the "L/R eigenmode reduction of the passive set — pure geometry, per campaign", `temporal_operator.py:326` provides `predict_vessel_currents`, and `imas_ambix/latent/passive_resistance.py:1` calibrates the passive L/R system from vacuum intervals; the plan names none of them.

findings.reason: §6 has a named owner to extend, and forking a second reduced model risks two current-diffusion owners drifting apart.
findings.text: §6's reduced traversal model ("passive circuits + current diffusion, no full free-boundary solve") re-implements machinery already owned by `imas_ambix/latent/current_diffusion.py:1` (1D flux-surface-averaged resistive current diffusion — the temporal prior, torch/fp64 implicit θ-scheme) and `imas_ambix/latent/transport.py:1` (learned flux-diffusion transport prior); `imas_ambix/physics/circuit.py` also exists for circuit dynamics.

findings.reason: a new fitting layer with no justification is exactly a thin wrapper; the honest change is an extension of `imas_ambix/calibration/` unless the plan states why not.
findings.text: §5's campaign tier ("machine-description corrections … fitted hierarchically across the labeled corpus and frozen") proposes a new hierarchical fitting layer without saying why the existing calibration machinery cannot host it: `imas_ambix/calibration/` already carries a corpus-compute / persistence / signals harness (`calibration/corpus_compute.py`, `calibration/persistence.py`).

findings.reason: the plan should name the single module that will hide the smoother, so the design can be judged deep or shallow before implementation.
findings.text: §5 defines substantial behaviour (two-tier estimation, 12–16 parameters per window, innovation classification across typed error sources, NK-convergence admission) but names no module or interface to hide it behind, so the design's depth is unstated and unverifiable; the only concrete artifact the section produced is `imas_ambix/closure/` (`closure/current_diffusion.py`, `closure/pressure.py`), which are two thin calibration wrappers rather than the deep estimator §5 describes.

findings.reason: the section must account for added interface surface in its own text under a zero-budget week, so the author would either name retirement or record the justification.
findings.text: with the supplied figures public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0, the plan adds public definitions in four places — `challenge/convention.py` (§2), the `thomson/` package (§3), the `closure/` package (§4) and the §7 amortizer — and no section names anything it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be; §2's own record (f-mfer-003) does claim the convention authority supersedes nova's `identify_source_cocos.py`, which is a retirement picked up on the nova side, but the ambix-side surfaces are unaccounted.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §5 names no module boundary at all: it specifies a two-tier estimator (campaign tier + shot tier, 12–16 parameters per window) purely in prose, so no interface is stated for the substantial behaviour it hides and `imas_ambix/closure/` (two thin calibration modules) is the only concrete artifact the section produced.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §5's windowed iterated ensemble smoother, §5's vessel-current eigenmodes and §6's passive-circuit + current-diffusion traversal each re-implement an owner that already exists (`statespace/nova_ensemble_estimator.py`, `latent/temporal_operator.py`, `latent/current_diffusion.py`); the plan also predicates §4/§5 on a nova free-boundary capability while `latent/gs_solve.py` already carries a free-boundary GS solver in-tree.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — supplied counts public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 (`challenge/convention.py`), §3 (`thomson/`), §4 (`closure/`) and §7 (amortizer) each add public definitions, and no section names anything it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2/§3 cite the machinery they extend (`challenge/convention.py` builds on `imas_ambix/cocos.py`; §5 mentions "the contract's integral-constraint policy", i.e. `fluxstate/`), but §5–§7 propose a smoother, a traversal model and an amortizer without naming the existing `statespace/` and `latent/` modules that already do those jobs.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §5's campaign tier and §6's reduced traversal model are described as new layers over fitting and current-diffusion machinery that already exists (`imas_ambix/calibration/`, `latent/current_diffusion.py`) with no statement of why those cannot be extended.
